pass_a_gloss: [...] the one who sets [you] in order toward piety through gospel oracles. [Lemma, Isaiah 57:5-8:] Those urging on to the idols under leafy trees, slaughtering their children in the ravines between the rocks. That is your portion, this your lot, and to those you poured out libations, and to those you brought up sacrifices. Upon these then will I not be angry? Upon a high and lofty mountain, there your bed, and there you brought up sacrifices, and behind the posts of your door you set your memorial. Having shown them killers of the Lord, he shows that the God-hating sickness in them, and the readiness for bloodshed, was not new in them, but indeed being in them from long and from above. For you are, he says, those in the times from above urging on to the idols under leafy trees. For although the law through Moses awarded them the useful things, and said expressly: You will worship the Lord your God, and him alone you will serve, they slid down into this [degree] of madness, rather of godlessness unrestrained and beyond every measure, so as to become craftsmen of idols, and to perform sacred rites to them, and to urge, or teach, others to worship under leafy trees, and to crown them with honours befitting God. This the God of all makes clear through the voice of Jeremiah, saying: You saw what the dwelling of Israel did to me; they went upon every high mountain and under every leafy tree, and committed fornication there. For seizing the tops of the mountains and the more flowering parts of the groves, they were building altars and precincts, and were bringing there sacrifices and libations to the unclean demons; and there are also those who did not spare their own children. At any rate Jechonias slaughtered his own son to the gods that are not. This God himself also said somewhere through one of the holy prophets, showing the cruelty of those accustomed to do such things: Sacrifice men; for calves have failed. You then are, he says, those urging on to the idols, slaughtering their children under leafy trees in the ravines between the rocks. What then upon these? That is your portion, this your lot. For you worshipped, he says, the vain things; and you will have such a portion, and the lot will be vain for you. Or perhaps he wishes to show that: You slaughtered their children in the ravines, he says. So that is your portion, this your lot, that is, you will be held in the equal evils, and the slaughter will become portion and lot for you. For what sort of cause? First because you became a child-killer, then because to unclean demons and lifeless idols you poured out libations, and to those you brought up sacrifices. Then upon these will I not be angr[y] [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … the One who would set you in order for godliness through the commands of the Gospel.

“You who urge others on to the idols under leafy trees, slaughtering their children in the ravines among the rocks: that is your portion, this is your lot. To them you poured out drink offerings, and to them you offered up sacrifices. Shall I not be angry at these things? On a high and lofty mountain, there is your bed, and there you brought up sacrifices; and behind the posts of your door you set your memorial” (Isaiah 57:5–8).

Having shown them to be killers of the Lord, he shows that their God-hating sickness and their readiness for bloodshed were nothing new in them, but had been in them for a long time, from of old. “For you are the ones,” he says, “who in the times of old urged others on to the idols under leafy trees.”

The Law given through Moses awarded them what was good for them and said plainly, “You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve” (Matthew 4:10; compare Deuteronomy 6:13). Yet they slid into such madness, or rather into a godlessness unrestrained and beyond all measure, that they became makers of idols, offered sacrifice to them, and urged others, that is, taught them, to worship under leafy trees and to crown the idols with honors fit only for God.

The God of all makes this plain through the voice of Jeremiah, saying: “Have you seen what the house of Israel has done to me? They went up on every high mountain and under every leafy tree, and there they prostituted themselves” (Jeremiah 3:6). For they took over the mountain peaks and the most flowering parts of the groves, built altars and sacred precincts, and brought sacrifices and drink offerings there to the unclean demons. And there were some who did not spare even their own children. Jechonias, indeed, slaughtered his own son to gods that do not exist.
God himself said this somewhere through one of the holy prophets, exposing the cruelty of those who were used to doing such things: “Sacrifice human beings, for the calves have run out” (Hosea 13:2).

“You, then,” he says, “are the ones who urge others on to the idols, slaughtering their children under leafy trees in the ravines among the rocks.” What then follows? “That is your portion, this is your lot.” “You have worshiped empty things,” he says, “and you will have a portion like them, and your lot will be empty.”

Or perhaps he means this: “You slaughtered their children in the ravines,” he says. “So that is your portion, this is your lot”; that is, you will be caught in the same evils, and slaughter will become your portion and lot. For what reason? First, because you became a killer of children; then, because you poured out drink offerings to unclean demons and lifeless idols, and offered up sacrifices to them. So then, at these things shall I not be angry …

choices.english: You who urge others on to the idols
choices.why: Cyril himself glosses παρακαλεῖν as 'teach others', so the lemma is 'urge others on', not 'call upon idols'.
Cyril's polemical charge against the people addressed; translated as written.

choices.english: You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve
choices.why: The wording of Matthew 4:10; the Septuagint of Deuteronomy 6:13 reads 'fear' and lacks 'alone'.
φρενοβλάβεια, damage of mind; Cyril then calls it godlessness beyond measure.
The name is Cyril's and is kept; Scripture records child sacrifice by Ahaz and Manasseh.
